summary: Make `board` a separate orchestrating capability. Its RSC surface authenticates the request, invokes board-owned application policy, and returns a renderable projection. The page must call this server code directly—not an internal Route Handler—consistent with Next.js App Router guidance for Server Components. [Next.js Server Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)

tree.purpose: Route-private RSC page; calls only `src/modules/board/rsc.ts` and renders the board projection.
Board RSC entrypoint; establishes explicit actor identity, invokes the board loader, and translates expected outcomes into renderable state/framework navigation.
Owns cross-capability policy: hide archived work-items, derive referenced label IDs, reject forbidden labels, attach visible label details, group by status, and produce the board projection.
Board-owned dependency contracts expressed in board vocabulary; imports no work-item or label types.
Private adapter from `work-items/server.ts` into the board port contract.
Private adapter from `labels/server.ts` into the board port contract, preserving visible/missing/forbidden reference states.
Explicit trusted server API for work-item reads; owns work-item persistence, validation, authorization, and ownership predicates.
Explicit trusted server API for label reads; owns label persistence, validation, authorization, and ownership predicates.

flows: `app/board/page.tsx` → `src/modules/board/rsc.ts` → authenticate request and establish `{ actorId, tenantId, scope }` → `board/application/load-board.ts`.
The board loader requests work-items through its board port; the private adapter calls `work-items/server.ts` with explicit identity. The work-items capability never imports board or labels.

The loader removes archived items, derives the label references from the remaining items, then requests those labels through the board port. The private adapter calls `labels/server.ts` with explicit identity.

The labels result must classify every requested reference as visible, missing, or forbidden without enumerating protected labels. Any forbidden reference produces a typed `forbidden` outcome; visible labels are attached and permitted missing-label behavior is applied explicitly.
The loader groups the resulting items by status and returns a board-owned render projection. `board/rsc.ts` maps it to the RSC page; no browser read, Server Action, or self-HTTP request is required.

decisions.rationale: Deleting it would move archival filtering, label authorization consequences, joining, and grouping into the route, failing the deletion test.

decisions.choice: Board depends on narrow `work-items/server.ts` and `labels/server.ts` surfaces through private adapters; work-items and labels remain independent.
decisions.rationale: This preserves independent persistence and changeability while preventing cross-capability imports and provider-shape leakage.

decisions.choice: Publish only `board/rsc.ts`, `work-items/server.ts`, and `labels/server.ts`; keep ports and adapters private.
decisions.rationale: Each surface has a named consumer and runtime boundary. No broad barrel or forwarding API is needed.

decisions.choice: `board/rsc.ts` establishes identity; each source capability rechecks its own policy; stores enforce tenant/ownership predicates.
decisions.rationale: Route protection or hidden UI is insufficient. Explicit identity prevents caller substitution and preserves defense in depth.

decisions.choice: Expected outcomes are typed values; unexpected contract, availability, and unknown failures propagate to the RSC boundary for one report and translation.
decisions.rationale: Source APIs and adapters remain silent. RSC maps unauthorized/forbidden/not-found outcomes to page state or framework navigation, while preserving redirect/not-found control flow outside generic catches.
The label request depends on the non-archived items’ references. This also avoids requesting labels for items that the board will hide.

decisions.choice: Test policy at the board application boundary with narrow fakes, source APIs at their trusted surfaces, and the page at the RSC boundary.
decisions.rationale: Assertions should cover observable policy and native channel outcomes rather than incidental call mechanics.

risks: A label that is missing must have an explicit product outcome; silently omitting forbidden labels is prohibited because it can conceal an authorization failure.
If work-item or label APIs return provider rows or implicit current-user identity, their server surfaces need translation and explicit identity before board integration.
The RSC page should use an error boundary/loading strategy appropriate to the product, but those route concerns remain under `app/` and must not absorb board policy.
Board projection changes may require coordinated contract tests, but the source capabilities remain independently deployable and independently testable.
